Twenty-eight comments

Josh, this sounds like a very ‘personalized’ version - lots of unusual twists and turns. Is it transcribed from a recording? If so, whose? The F-naturals (or rather, absence of F#) is an interesting touch. I’d have called it G mixolydian, rather than C major, though.

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on February 26th, 2002.

This is, in fact, transcribed from a recording. However, sadly, I can’t remember the name of the recording.
My friend Phil plays it this way and this is how he taught it to me.

“Tom Ward’s Downfall” ~ another take

As with this transcription, F natural doesn’t fit except to grate, any pass from one thing to another that you could slip an F into would be sharp… So, this tune is in G Major, as in this alternate take on it, not C and not mixolydian:

Key signature: G Major

the Mourne Mountains, X:11

This setting from a recording of Mrs. Molly Myers Murphy of Glencollins, Ballydesmond, Co. Cork. She likely got it from Tom Billy Murphy, the blind fiddle master that taught her during her youth in Co. Kerry.
